quote: However, "the concept of the pronephros does not apply to the human embryo" (Torrey, 1954).
note: Contradicts the table outright, not by a stage but in kind. Two rows assert the pronephros exists in Homo sapiens from CS9 to CS12; the primary source says the concept does not apply to this species at all. What the book does place here is the nephrogenic cord differentiating from intermediate mesoderm. Both pronephros rows should be withdrawn or restated as the nephrogenic cord rather than shifted.

quote: A ureteric bud may possibly be present in some specimens (Wells, 1954, fig. 4), although further confirmation is needed.
note: The table asserts `existence starts during CS13`. The source will not commit to CS13 in any form: it hedges twice in one sentence and names a single figure in a single paper as the basis. This supports at most RO:0002496 (starts during or after) at CS13, with the firm bound at CS14.

quote: Internal: the ventral pancreas (if not detectable earlier) is distinguishable at stages 14 and 15; right and left lung sacs grow dorsad; the ureteric bud acquires a metanephrogenic cap; future cerebral hemispheres and cerebellar plates begin to be visible.
note: The first unhedged statement that the bud exists, and in the stage summary rather than a caveated aside. CS14 is the defensible start bound. The same sentence also supports metanephric cap at CS14, which the table already has.

quote: The mesonephros shows epithelial plaques in the visceral layer of the glomerular capsule and hence can produce urine (Silverman, 1969).
note: The table's row says the mesonephros is 'functional from CS11'. This is the source's only statement about mesonephric function and it puts urine production at CS17, six stages later. CS11 is where nephric vesicles first appear, which is presence, not function. The existence bound at CS11 may still be right; the word 'functional' in the evidence text is not.

quote: The metanephros, which is now reniform, is still sacral in level.
note: The first time the source names the metanephros as such. Corroborates rather than contradicts the table's CS14 start, which rests on the ureteric bud acquiring its metanephrogenic cap at CS14; 'now reniform' at CS16 reads as a structure already under way. Recorded as `present` because a first naming is not an onset.

quote: Collecting tubules develop from the calices at stages 17 and 18 (fig. 18-14).
note: The table ends the ureteric bud at CS16, on the grounds that it 'has branched into the collecting system by CS16'. The source puts collecting-tubule development at stages 17 and 18, so the end bound looks two stages early. At CS16 the source has the ureteric pelvis only just dividing into rostral and caudal poles.
